response.answer: No, the compliance deadline did not change. Document 2025-03118 (90 FR 10592, published 2025-02-25) delayed the effective date of the 'healthy' claim final rule (2024-29957, 89 FR 106064) from February 25, 2025 to April 28, 2025, in accordance with the Presidential memorandum 'Regulatory Freeze Pending Review.' However, the document explicitly states: 'We note that the compliance date remains unchanged at this time.' The compliance date of February 25, 2028, as originally stated in 2024-29957 (89 FR 106064), remains in effect. This means regulated parties must conform to the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim requirements under 21 CFR 101.65(d) by February 25, 2028, even though the rule text did not legally take effect until April 28, 2025.

answer_rows.product: All products bearing a 'healthy' nutrient content claim
answer_rows.required_change: Products bearing the 'healthy' claim (or derivative terms) must meet the new food-group-equivalent and nutrients-to-limit criteria established in 21 CFR 101.65(d)

response.answer: Under the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim rule (89 FR 106064, codified at 21 CFR 101.65(d)), a food that does not qualify for one of the automatic exemptions (e.g., single-ingredient foods from encouraged food groups, or water/tea/coffee) must meet two main criteria to bear the 'healthy' claim: (1) **Food Group Equivalent (FGE) requirement** — the food must contain a specified amount of at least one food group equivalent from the food groups encouraged by the Dietary Guidelines (vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fat-free/low-fat dairy, lean meat/seafood/eggs/beans/peas/lentils/nuts/seeds), as defined in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(2); and (2) **Nutrient-to-Limit (NTL) requirement** — the food must not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients (21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v)). This two-pronged approach is summarized in the background section of 90 FR 10592 (document 2025-03118), which states the rule 'requires that, to bear a claim subject to the rule, individual food products, mixed products, main dishes, and meals must meet FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients.' The preamble to the final rule (89 FR 106064) further explains that the FGE criteria ensure foods contain beneficial nutrients from nutrient-dense food groups (21 CFR 101.65(d)(2)–(3)), while the NTL criteria limit nutrients that should be consumed in moderation.

answer_rows.required_change: Food must (1) contain a qualifying amount of a food group equivalent (FGE) from dietary-guideline-encouraged food groups, AND (2) not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium (NTLs based on % Daily Value)

response.answer: The 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim is governed by 21 CFR 101.65(d). This section defines the general nutritional claims paragraph covering labeling claims that are implied nutrient content claims because they suggest that a food may help consumers maintain healthy dietary practices due to its nutrient content. The general framework for implied nutrient content claims (including 'healthy') is set out in 21 CFR 101.13(b)(2)(ii), which defines an implied nutrient content claim as one that 'suggests that a food, because of its nutrient content, may be useful in maintaining healthy dietary practices, where there is also implied or explicit information about the nutrition content of the food (e.g., "healthy")' (21 CFR 101.13(b)(2)(ii) as revised by document 2024-29957, 89 FR 106064). The specific criteria a food must meet to bear the 'healthy' claim are found in 21 CFR 101.65(d). The final rule updating the definition of 'healthy' was published on December 27, 2024 (89 FR 106064, document 2024-29957), with an effective date of April 28, 2025 (as delayed by document 2025-03118), and a compliance date of February 25, 2028.

answer_rows.trigger: Final rule 2024-29957 (89 FR 106064) revising 21 CFR 101.65(d) definition of 'healthy'
answer_rows.required_change: Products must meet the updated food-group-equivalent-based criteria in revised 21 CFR 101.65(d)(3) (including nutrient limits in tables 2 and 3) to bear the 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim

response.answer:
The Red No. 3 order (90 FR 4628, Doc. 2025-00830, published 2025-01-16) changes two CFR provisions in 21 CFR Part 74, but they do NOT all change on the same day:

1. **21 CFR 74.303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for food use): Amendatory instruction 2 removes this section, and amendatory instruction 3 revises § 74.1303 (to incorporate identity/specifications from § 74.303 before it disappears). Both take effect **January 15, 2027** (2025-00830#0000; timeline-facts).

2. **21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs): Amendatory instruction 4 removes this section, effective **January 18, 2028** (2025-00830#0002; timeline-facts).

Specifically, the amendatory instructions are (2025-00830#0002):
- Instruction 2: Remove § 74.303 — effective January 15, 2027.
- Instruction 3: Revise § 74.1303 (adding identity and specifications from § 74.303) — effective January 15, 2027.
- Instruction 4: Remove § 74.1303 — effective January 18, 2028.

The order sets no separate compliance date for any provision. Because this is a revocation (not a new requirement), the operative deadline is derived from the effective date: once the listing is removed, any food or drug containing FD&C Red No. 3 is adulterated (2025-00830#0021). The administrative stay that began February 18, 2025, was lifted August 5, 2026, and the original effective dates of January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, are confirmed (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920#0000).

answer_rows.product: Any food (including dietary supplements) containing FD&C Red No. 3
answer_rows.required_change: Reformulate to eliminate FD&C Red No. 3 from all food products; after effective date the color additive is no longer listed and its use renders food adulterated

answer_rows.product: Any ingested drug containing FD&C Red No. 3
answer_rows.required_change: Reformulate to eliminate FD&C Red No. 3 from all ingested drug products; after effective date the color additive is no longer listed and its use renders the drug adulterated

response.answer: Under 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2), a 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must be made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with one specific carve-out: § 101.13(h) is excepted when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of § 101.65. Section 101.13(h) is the disclosure requirement that would otherwise mandate a statement such as 'See nutrition information for ___ content' when a food exceeds specified levels of fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, or sodium. This disclosure requirement does not apply to foods bearing the 'healthy' claim under § 101.65(d). All other provisions of § 101.13 — including requirements on claim type size (§ 101.13(f)), the general prohibition on nutrient content claims unless made in accordance with subpart D (§ 101.13(b)), and the requirement that the food be labeled with nutrition information — remain applicable.

answer_rows.trigger: Use of 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim on label or labeling
answer_rows.required_change: Ensure compliance with all general requirements of 21 CFR 101.13 (e.g., type size, labeling requirements, general claim principles) except § 101.13(h) disclosure statements, which are carved out for 'healthy' claims made under § 101.65(d)
